title: How the Google algorithm works in 2025
description: How the Google algorithm works in 2025 : there is no single algorithm, but three stages (crawling, indexing, ranking) and dozens of systems working together on ranking, some publicly...
body:
How the Google algorithm works in 2025: there is no single algorithm, but three stages (crawling, indexing, ranking) and dozens of systems working together on ranking, some publicly described by Google in its ranking systems guide. This guide explains each stage and what you control, the main systems and what they do, what changed in 2025 (more core updates, expanded generated answers) and what it means for a company site in Romania.

We write from daily practice with Search Console across dozens of sites, where the effects of these systems are visible in the figures, even though their weights remain unpublished.

How the Google algorithm works in 2025

Stage 1: crawling

Googlebot discovers addresses (from links, sitemaps and known addresses) and downloads them, with a site budget dependent on server speed and Google's interest in the site. Pages are rendered (JavaScript executed) in a separate step. What you control: accessibility (robots.txt, firewall, speed), the sitemap, internal links and the absence of unnecessary addresses; details are in the article on crawl budget.

Stage 2: indexing

Google analyses the page (text, headings, images, structured data, links), chooses the canonical among duplicates, determines the language and country, and stores it in the index, or does not (thin, duplicate or blocked content). What you control: content, canonical, noindex, hreflang and quality; reasons for non-indexing are in the guide to coverage reports.

Stage 3: ranking

For every search, ranking systems select relevant pages from the index and order them within fractions of a second, based on hundreds of signals grouped into a few families: query meaning, content relevance, quality (expertise, authority, trust), usability (speed, mobile, HTTPS) and context (location, language, history). Weights vary by search type: freshness matters for news, distance for local services and trust for health.

Ranking systems published by Google

SystemWhat it doesWhat it means for you
RankBrain (2015)machine learning to understand new queries and word meaningswrite for meaning, not exact matches
Neural matching, BERT (2019), MUMunderstanding context and subtleties in queries and pages, across languagesanswer the real question in natural language
Helpful content system (2022, integrated into core since 2024)assesses whether the site is made for people, at site levelremove content without value; the proportion matters
Reviews system (integrated since 2023)favours reviews with first-hand experience, evidence and comparisonsyour own reviews, with photographs and tests
Link analysis (PageRank and successors)links as votes, weighted by relevance and trustearned links, not bought ones
Freshnessfavours recent content for time-sensitive queriesupdate what changes; do not change the date without changing content
Passage rankingassesses sections of the page, not just the wholeclear subheadings, answers beneath each
Spam systems (SpamBrain)detect and demote spam, including manipulated links and scaled contentfollow the policies; there are no lasting shortcuts
Page experienceCore Web Vitals, HTTPS, mobile, no intrusive pop-upstechnical hygiene, not strategy
Local, personalisation, deduplicationresults based on location and history, without duplicatesGoogle Business Profile; pages based on intent, not variants

The complete list and official descriptions are in the ranking systems guide in Search Central; Google updates the page when it retires or integrates systems.

What changed in 2025

  • Core updates: several throughout the year (March, June and subsequent ones), with two- to three-week rollouts in which quality systems (including the former helpful content system) were recalibrated; sites with a high proportion of generic pages continued to lose, while those with experience and real authors gained. Measuring the effect is covered in the article on measuring the impact of an update.
  • The March 2024 spam policies (scaled content, site reputation, expired domains) were applied throughout 2025, with manual actions and spam updates.
  • AI Overviews expanded to more markets and search types, while AI Mode launched as a conversational interface; cited sources are chosen by the same ranking systems, but the format reduces informational clicks; the effect is described in the article on AI Mode and organic traffic.
  • Retirement of the crawl rate limit setting in Search Console and the Mobile-Friendly test; Google decides the pace itself, while mobile is assessed through Core Web Vitals.
  • Public clarifications that there is no "E-E-A-T score" and that user interactions are used in aggregate, not per page; what is known is in the article on interaction signals.

What it means for a company site

  1. Accessible and technically clean: no blocks, fast on mobile, with unique addresses; a requirement, not an advantage.
  2. Intent-based pages: one page per need, with the answer at the top and subheadings enabling passage ranking.
  3. Site-level quality: the proportion of useful pages; consolidating and removing weak ones matters as much as new content.
  4. Demonstrated trust: authors, sources, identity, genuine reviews; the signals are described in the article on why E-E-A-T matters.
  5. Earned links from relevant sources, a few per month.
  6. Local: a complete Google Business Profile, for local systems.
  7. Updating what changes and patience with updates: effects arrive in two to six months.

An example: the same query, three systems

The search "how much does a brochure website cost" from Romania. Query understanding systems classify it as commercial-informational, in Romanian, without strong local intent. Passage ranking brings forward pages that have an answer with price ranges under a subheading, even if the whole page is about something else. The helpful content system demotes sites with dozens of generic articles "about prices" without figures. Freshness favours pages updated in 2025, because prices change. The result: on the first page, service pages with displayed prices and updated guides with cost tables; absent are long articles saying "it depends on many factors". On our own pages we added price indications after carrying out this analysis.

How the systems are trained

Google uses human raters who score samples of results using public guidelines (the quality raters' guidelines); the scores do not change positions but measure whether a system change improved results, and train the models. Similarly, aggregated user interactions indicate whether the proposed order satisfied users. The consequence: systems evolve towards what people consider useful and trustworthy, and the raters' guidelines are the best public description of the target; the chapters on quality and E-E-A-T are required reading for anyone writing for the web.

Persistent myths

  • "Keyword density": the systems understand meaning; repetition does not help and, in excess, harms.
  • "Google penalises AI content": it penalises content without value, regardless of the tool; details are in the article on how Google detects automatically generated content.
  • "Domain age matters": not directly; what has accumulated on it matters.
  • "Analytics bounce rate is a factor": Google does not read Analytics for ranking.
  • "There is a trick": systems are trained to reward what people reward; tricks work until the next update.

How to track changes

Google's ranking status page for announced updates, the Search Central blog for clarifications, the ranking systems guide for the current inventory, and Search Console for the effect on your own site, with comparisons over equal periods and groups of pages. Do not follow rumours about "secret factors"; follow your own figures. What specifically happened with the 2025 updates and what comes next in 2026 is in the guide to Google algorithm updates in 2026, while diagnosing a site against these systems is the opening part of the SEO audit.

What you can do this week

Three checks with a direct effect on how systems see the site: the indexing report (what does not enter the index and why), the first two sentences under every subheading on commercial pages (do they answer directly?) and the about page with authors (is there an identity?). Each corresponds to a stage or system above, and correcting them needs no budget, just an afternoon; the steps are in the guide to optimising a site step by step.

Frequently asked questions

  1. How many signals does Google use? Google has said "hundreds"; the number does not matter because you cannot optimise them individually; you can optimise the families above.
  2. Is the algorithm the same in Romania as in the US? The systems are the same; weights and data differ by language and market, and some features (AI Mode) arrive later.
  3. Can I find out why a page dropped? Not directly; you can compare it with pages that rose for the same queries and check technical and quality signals.
  4. How often does the algorithm change? Daily, through thousands of small changes; announced changes come a few times a year through core and spam updates.
